I grew up in Oulu, I have deliberately chosen to build my career here, and I would rather put the case directly than assume the answer is no.

I am available to meet at your convenience.

Satu Lehtinen

application.cover_letter_markdown:
After twenty-four years at Vireo Sensor Systems, I have been thinking carefully about where the next part of my career should go. The Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara is the first opening that has felt like a genuine fit for the kind of work I want to keep doing, and for the direction I want to move in.

My career at Vireo has been almost entirely in audio and sensor signal processing. Hearing instruments, medical-device sensor boards, and the calibration and test infrastructure that supports them. It has been steady, technically deep work, and I have valued the breadth it gave me. Over two decades I have gone from embedded firmware through production tooling to RF characterisation, and I contributed signal processing work for an EORA subcontract that involved an airborne instrument validation campaign. But Vireo is a smaller company now than it was ten years ago, and the range of projects has narrowed. I want to stay hands-on as an engineer, and I want to work on instruments and systems that push further than what I have been doing.

The reason I think this is a natural step rather than a stretch: my Applied Physics degree from Tammerkoski University gave me a strong grounding in electromagnetic theory, Fourier analysis, and statistical signal processing. Those are the foundations I have drawn on in every role since — the mathematics of sensor arrays, noise modelling, spectral estimation. The specific application domains have changed, but the underlying theory has not, and it is the theory side I find most rewarding. Kaikuvaara's work in remote-sensing instruments is a domain I have not worked in directly, but it sits on the same mathematical foundations, and I am comfortable that my depth of practical experience would transfer without a long ramp-up period.

I have also contributed to a few published articles and technical reports over the years, though I would describe my publication activity as modest and secondary to the hands-on engineering.

Practically, I am a Finnish citizen, I spent eighteen months at Vireo's Oulu office in 2019–2020 and know the city well. My notice period at Vireo is three months.

I do not have experience in remote sensing specifically. What I do have is a quarter-century of building, testing, and shipping signal processing systems in C and Python, working with RF hardware on a real test bench, and solving problems under real engineering constraints. That depth is what I would bring.

I would be glad to discuss this further.

Elina Turunen

application.cover_letter_markdown:
I completed my Master's in Electrical Engineering at Tammerkoski University in 2024 and have been working at Baltic Sensor Networks since January this year. I realise the posting is for a senior role and that I have roughly one year of professional experience. I am applying anyway, because Kaikuvaara is the kind of company I want to work for, and I would rather explain that directly than wait for a junior posting that may not come.

My thesis at Tampere dealt with adaptive noise cancellation for industrial vibration sensors — concretely, the problem of monitoring drive-train health in paper mills using accelerometer data that is noisy, non-stationary, and drifts with temperature. I implemented three adaptive filtering approaches, benchmarked them against real mill data, and built the full simulation pipeline myself. It was not glamorous, but it forced me to understand what happens to filtering algorithms when the textbook assumptions break down: windowing artefacts, convergence-rate sensitivity, the gap between a result on clean data and one that survives in the field. The thesis was awarded with distinction, which mattered to me because the examiners were practitioners, not just academics.

At Baltic Sensor Networks my day-to-day involves writing embedded DSP modules in C++ for ground-station receiver boards on Xilinx Zynq SoC platforms. Decimation filters, IF-to-baseband conversion, and the test infrastructure to validate the signal chain end to end. The company is small, and I have been given more hands-on responsibility than I expected for someone this early in their career. I have come to appreciate how different it is to write code that runs reliably on real hardware under timing constraints versus code that merely compiles and passes a simulation. That gap is something I find genuinely interesting to work in.

I am applying to Kaikuvaara because remote-sensing instruments sit at the intersection of the things I care about most: real-time signal processing, sensor systems, and hardware that has to work in conditions you cannot fully predict. The instruments you build are the kind of engineering problem that drew me into this field in the first place, and I would like to work somewhere that operates at that level of ambition. I visited Oulu for a university project a few years ago and came away with a good impression of the city and its engineering community.

On the theory side, I am comfortable with estimation and filtering concepts including Kalman filtering, though I have not yet had the opportunity to apply them in an industrial setting.

I do not pretend to be a senior engineer. If there is scope to discuss a more junior entry point, or if the team can accommodate someone who would grow into the full scope of the role, I would be glad to have that conversation.

Andrei Popescu

status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Kaisa Laine
kaisa.laine@mail.example | +358 00 000 0103

Education

MSc Engineering Physics
Kallavesi University of Technology (formerly Nuuksio Institute of Technology), 2007

Experience

Signal Processing Engineer
Aurinko Avionics, Espoo
2008 – present

- Contributed to signal processing subsystems for airborne radar and optical instrument products across multiple EORA-contracted programmes
- Participated in flight qualification and acceptance testing campaigns for two airborne instrument payloads delivered to EORA (2012 and 2018)
- All technical documentation, design reviews, and customer communication conducted in English as the company's working language for international space programmes

Projects

**Phased-array beamforming for airborne SAR receiver** (2014 – 2017)
Designed a beamforming algorithm for the receive chain of an 8-element X-band synthetic aperture radar antenna. The work covered sidelobe suppression, null placement for interference rejection, and beam-steering angle optimisation for off-nadir imaging. Implemented in MATLAB for prototype validation, then delivered the design specification for firmware integration.

**Embedded DSP for optical-instrument readout** (2018 – 2020)
Wrote embedded DSP firmware in C for a TI TMS320C6678 multi-core processor, handling real-time data reduction from an optical detector array operating at 200 MS/s. The firmware implemented baseline subtraction, noise blanking, and packet framing for downlink, all within a 5 W power envelope.

**Post-flight data processing toolkit** (2020 – present)
Built and maintained a Python-based data processing toolkit for post-flight analysis of instrument telemetry. Handles data ingestion, calibration correction, and quick-look product generation. Maintained with pytest and used across Aurinko's Espoo and Oulu offices. Includes a CLI documented for non-developer users.

**CubeSat imager signal-chain design** (2022 – 2023)
Designed a miniaturised signal chain for a CubeSat imager payload, drawing directly on the signal theory, statistical methods, and numerical analysis foundations of my Engineering Physics MSc from Kallavesi. The design covered detector front-end through A/D conversion, noise reduction, and lossless compression.

**Oulu facility integration support** (2023 – 2024)
Provided six months of on-site signal processing support at Aurinko's Oulu facility during integration and environmental testing of a multi-spectral sensor payload. Close day-to-day coordination with the Oulu-based systems engineering team.

Skills

Signal processing algorithm design, embedded firmware (C, TI DSPs), Python, MATLAB, airborne instrument systems, SAR processing, data reduction, optical detector readout
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Remote-sensing instruments are what I have spent my career building, and Kaikuvaara is the company in Finland that does this work best. That is the short version of why I am applying.

I have been at Aurinko Avionics since 2008, working on signal processing for airborne and spaceborne instrument payloads. Over that time I have designed beamforming algorithms for SAR receivers, written embedded DSP firmware in C for optical-instrument readout at 200 MS/s, and built a Python data processing toolkit that the analysis team uses across two offices. The work I find most compelling is the transition from algorithm design to flight-qualified hardware — the moment when you discover which of your design assumptions actually hold when the instrument is running on a real platform, collecting real data, under real thermal and power constraints.

I have been part of two EORA-contracted airborne instrument programmes that went through full flight qualification, in 2012 and 2018. Those experiences shaped how I think about instrument signal processing. The constraints of a flight platform — fixed power budgets, radiation tolerance, no opportunity for a firmware update once the instrument is airborne — force you to be very deliberate about what goes into the design and very thorough about how you test it. The most recent programme involved an optical instrument payload, and it reinforced something I had already learned from the 2012 radar campaign: the hardest problems in instrument signal processing are the ones you do not see coming until the real data arrives.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara specifically is the focus. Aurinko is an avionics company that happens to build instruments as one of several product lines; Kaikuvaara is an instruments company. That difference shows up in how much depth and continuity the instrument engineering group gets, and in the career development available to someone who wants to stay technical. I am not looking for a management path. I want to keep designing signal processing systems for instruments that fly, and I think Kaikuvaara is the best place in Finland to do that.

If you are looking for someone who can step in and contribute across algorithm design and embedded implementation, with a real understanding of what flight-qualified instrument engineering requires, I would welcome the chance to discuss it.

Kaisa Laine

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Oulu has been on my mind as a place to work for a while now. I have spent several stints at Aurinko's test facility there over the years, and each time I come away thinking that the concentration of instrument and photonics engineering in that city is something I would like to be part of on a permanent basis rather than as a visitor on a four-month test assignment.

I have been at Aurinko Avionics since 2015, working on signal processing for satellite and airborne instrument payloads. My work has covered the full chain from algorithm design through embedded firmware to production test tooling. I have contributed to three satellite payload programmes, including a spaceborne scatterometer where I was responsible for the data-reduction firmware, and on the embedded side I wrote C firmware for a multispectral imager readout running on a TI C6678 DSP. More recently I built a Python calibration pipeline that the team uses daily for bench-level characterisation of payload electronics.

I took a sabbatical in 2020–2021 for personal travel. It shows as a gap in my timeline and I mention it only because it is visible. I came back to Aurinko in late 2021 and resumed my work without difficulty.

What interests me about Kaikuvaara is the company's position in the Oulu engineering community. The RF and photonics cluster there — the university research groups, Suvanto, and the companies building instruments for space programmes — is dense in a way that few places in Finland match. Aurinko does solid work, but it is fundamentally an avionics company that builds instruments as one line of business. Kaikuvaara is an instruments company, and I would expect the depth of the engineering team and the breadth of problems to reflect that difference. The problems you are working on — phased-array signal processing for SAR, payload electronics for remote sensing — are the area where I have the most experience and the most energy.

I have also done hands-on RF front-end characterisation, most recently on an L-band scatterometer receiver, and I have designed phased-array beamforming algorithms for an airborne SAR payload. These are areas I could contribute to from day one. I hold EU work authorisation and could start after a standard notice period. A permanent move to Oulu is something I would actively welcome.

I would be glad to discuss the role further.

Emma Popescu
